title: On-Prem Inventory → Operations Mapping (feasibility notes)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures the inventory we collected during the customer workshop (01/10–01/12), maps those items to operational responsibilities, and flags feasibility concerns specific to an air-gapped / highly restricted on-prem deployment. Intended audience: solutions-eng, infra-eng, customer infra contact, and CSM.

High-level customer context (short):
- Sector: regulated medical devices (EMR-adjacent).
- Rationale: data residency + regulatory controls require no egress.
- Desired outcome: run Redwood Private with model serving in their datacenter, with periodic controlled syncs for model/artifact updates.
- Customer environment: 2 datacenters (primary + DR), separated by low-latency WAN (10ms), strict egress firewall policies, internal PKI and HSM for key storage.

Workshop attendees (sticky notes):
- Customer: IT Ops lead (Sandra), Network lead (Oded), Security architect (Marcus), App Platform (Rohit)
- Redwood: Aisha (solutions lead), Marco (infra), Luis (serving runtime SME), Priya (security)
content_addendum:
Inventory snapshot (collected):
- Hardware: 3 x racks per site available; current preference is to provision 4x compute nodes initially. Nodes: Dell R750xd equivalent, 2x CPUs, 512GB RAM, 2 x 1.6TB NVMe (local cache), 200TB NFS (central) per site. GPU options: customer currently has a mixed pool: 4x A100 40GB (procured but not racked), potential to add 2x H100 in Q2.
- Networking: 10Gb internal fabric, spine-leaf; public egress blocked by default, outbound only through vetted proxy appliances. Internal DNS and split-horizon.
- Storage: S3-compatible object store (on-prem Ceph cluster) with bucket policies; weekly snapshots to immutable tape vault (compliance).
- Identity & Keys: Internal PKI, HashiCorp Vault (enterprise) available in both DCs. HSM provided via network HSM appliances; customer requires secrets never be exported in plaintext.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes 1.25 (self-managed) in both datacenters. Airgap images must be imported via internal registry.
- Monitoring/Observability: Prometheus + Grafana in-house; logs aggregated to Splunk with offline ingestion windows.
- Change control: Maintenance windows defined Tuesday 02:00–06:00 local, emergency change board required for any system-level upgrades.

Constraints called out by customer (red):
- Zero egress: no outbound model downloads or telemetry to hosted endpoints without explicit, signed deployment window.
- No arbitrary downloadable binaries: all images and installers must be validated, checksummed, and imported via an approved channel.
- KMS/HSM policy: private keys originate in HSM; Redwood cannot bring keys out of HSM.
- Audit & retention: audit logs must be retained for 7 years; all access must be logged with SSO identity.
- FIPS/NIAP guidance: certain workflows will require FIPS-validated crypto where possible.

Operational mapping (how each inventory item affects Redwood deliverables):
- GPU provisioning: Redwood can provide a recommended node-to-GPU mapping and optimized model bundle sizes. Ops impact: need SSH access to cluster bootstrap nodes and bare-metal inventory; timeline depends on rack provisioning (4–6 weeks if new hardware).
- Image delivery: customer will host an internal registry (Harbor). Redwood must package images and deliver via signed tarball + sha256 for import. Ops impact: create an offline image packaging script and verification checklist.
- Model updates: periodic model bundles (quantized variants) shipped as encrypted tarballs. Customer will stage them in internal object store. Ops impact: define a draconian rollback and validation test for each model update (unit prompts provided by Redwood).
- Secrets and keys: Redwood runtime must integrate with customer Vault/HSM via network CA. Ops impact: add Vault auth plugin and document KMS integration steps; cannot require export of root keys.

Feasibility observations and tradeoffs (quick):
- Full parity with hosted monitoring is not feasible in strictest airgap: streaming token-level telemetry needs redesign to local buffer + push windows. Tradeoff: lose near-real-time unit cost visibility; gain compliance.
- Quantized models (4-bit / 8-bit) reduce hardware footprint but require validated pipelines for quantization reproducibility. Tradeoff: lower infra cost vs extra validation during model updates.
- Rollouts: can do canary within cluster by traffic-splitting layer, but cross-site rollback semantics must be explicit due to replication windows.

Minimal deployment profile (recommended starting POC):
- Site A (primary): 4 nodes with GPUs (4x A100 40GB) + 3 control VMs; 2 x 25Gb NICs; 50TB local cache + mounted S3 for models.
- Site B (DR): 2 nodes with GPUs (or lower spec) + control VMs for warm standby.
- Software: Kubernetes 1.25, Harbor internal registry, Ceph S3, Vault + HSM, Prometheus/Grafana (local).
- Network: open ports list documented below; default-deny outbound; internal registry accessible from cluster only.

Critical network ports (initial list we validated with Oded):
- Internal registry (Harbor): 443 (HTTPS), 5000 (optional)
- Kubernetes API: 6443 (control-plane access authenticated)
- Object storage (S3-compatible): 443
- Redis/KV (internal caching if used): 6379 (if internal only)
- Runtime health checks: 10250 (kubelet), custom agent 8777 (if enabled)
Notes: all connections MUST be mutual-TLS.

Runbook considerations (ops):
- Bootstrapping images: produce a signed bundle + verification script. Customer will import and scan before deployment.
- Upgrades: apply-in-place upgrades only during change window; major runtime upgrades require offline acceptance testing by customer.
- Backups: model bundles stored in S3 with object-lock enabled; backups copied to tape weekly.
- Incident response: create a staged offline triage playbook — capture dumps locally, transmit only via approved secure courier when required.

Open questions (needs customer answers):
1) Are customers willing to provision a transient bastion with restricted egress for one-time bootstrap (preferred)? (Asked 01/11)
2) Does internal compliance allow checksums/signatures only, or is an allowlist of binary hashes required?
3) Can we rely on scheduled manual windows for telemetry extraction to Redwood hosted systems for billing/usage, or must usage accounting be fully local and provided as CSV?
4) HSM integration: do we have network access to HSM admin plane, or must all CSR/key ops be offline?

Immediate next steps + action owners (short):
- Aisha: produce signed image packaging script and checklist (deliverable: signed-image-v0.1.tar.gz) — due 2025-01-20.
- Marco: draft minimal infra diagram with exact port flows and network ACLs (deliverable: network-matrix.pdf) — due 2025-01-18.
- Luis: prepare model validation prompt set for SANITY checks and regression thresholds (deliverable: model-validation-suite.zip) — due 2025-01-22.
- Priya: draft security integration doc for Vault/HSM and FIPS considerations (deliverable: vault-integration-notes.md) — due 2025-01-21.
- Customer (Sandra): confirm bastion and image import process; provide bullet answers to Open Questions by 2025-01-17.

Risks & mitigation map (short bullets):
- Risk: Image import failure due to different distro/parity. Mitigation: provide both container and VM images; preflight scripts.
- Risk: Telemetry restrictions prevent billing. Mitigation: export local accounting CSV and scheduled manual upload process.
- Risk: HSM policy prevents runtime from deriving keys. Mitigation: use key-wrapping with ephemeral keys provisioned by customer HSM.

Loose notes / things to keep in mind:
- Keep all artifacts PATTERNED: tar.gz + sha256 + OEM-signed manifest.
- We should prototype an entirely local-only demo with telemetry stubbed out to show runtime behavior to Security team.
- Consider a two-phase POC: Phase 1 = install and run basic inference with canned prompts; Phase 2 = model update automation + rollback + cost telemetry extraction.

Appendix: references and checklist excerpts (for ops):
- Checklist: hostnames and FQDNs required, cert CN policy, internal CA thumbprint, Harbor admin account creation, object store bucket name and policy, kubelet node labels for scheduling GPUs.
- Quick acceptance criteria for POC: 1) successful inference tests with 95th percentile latency < defined SLO on sample prompts; 2) model update can be pushed and validated without manual host access; 3) audit logs captured and exported to customer Splunk for a 7-day window.

Status summary (one-liner):
POC is feasible but requires image-signing tooling, clear HSM integration constraints, and an agreed manual telemetry/billing path.
